question: Should acpx intentionally make structured argv mandatory for Windows agent launches now, accepting that raw commands, direct .sh wrappers, and legacy custom sessions without saved argv require migration or recreation?
rationale: The patch is a plausible fix for ambiguous Windows command parsing, but it changes a public configuration, CLI, embedded-registry, and persisted-session compatibility contract rather than preserving the formerly accepted raw-command path.

options.title: Approve the explicit Windows contract
options.body: Keep the fail-closed argv requirement, provided the PR adds real Windows proof and clearly documents migration for config, `--agent`, embedded registries, and existing sessions.

options.title: Preserve a compatibility path
options.body: Retain an opt-in or supported legacy Windows launch route while structured argv becomes the recommended path, accepting more long-term command-parsing complexity.

options.title: Pause for a narrower design
options.body: Defer the broad contract change and land only a narrower fix once maintainers choose how external .sh-wrapper integrations should migrate.

recommendation.title: Approve the explicit Windows contract
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed argv requirement, provided the PR adds real Windows proof and clearly documents migration for config, `--agent`, embedded registries, and existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposed commits span the contract, migration, and Windows spawn boundaries that require the product decision.
